user_input: Who desides the order when rules happen at the same time in Warhamer 40,000?
reference: If two or more rules are to be resolved at the same time during the battle, the player whose turn it is chooses the order. If it occurs before or after the battle, or at the start or end of a battle round, the players roll off and the winner decides the order.
reference_contexts:
SEQUENCING
While playing Warhammer 40,000, you'll occasionally find that two or more rules are to be resolved at the same time. If this occurs during the battle, the player whose turn it is chooses the order. If this occurs before or after the battle, or at the start or end of a battle round, the players roll off and the winner decides the order in which those rules are resolved.

user_input: can you tell me if a Vehicle unit is still allowed for shooting when they are in Engagement Range of enemy units?
reference: Yes, Monster and Vehicle units are eligible to shoot in their controlling player's Shooting phase even while they are within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units.
reference_contexts:
BIG GUNS NEVER TIRE
Monsters and war engines can dispense death from afar even as they trample the masses before them.
Monster and Vehicle units are eligible to shoot in their controlling player's Shooting phase even while they are within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units. Ranged weapons equipped by Monster and Vehicle units can target one or more of the enemy units they are within Engagement Range of, even if other friendly units are also within Engagement Range of the same enemy unit. Each time a Monster or Vehicle model makes a ranged attack, if its unit was within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units when it selected its targets, unless that attack is made with a Pistol (pg 25), subtract 1 from that attack's Hit roll.
You can select an enemy Monster or Vehicle unit within Engagement Range of one or more units from your army as a target of ranged weapons. Each time a model from your army makes a ranged attack against such a target, unless that attack is made with a Pistol, subtract 1 from that attack's Hit roll.

user_input: Me and my opponent need to know how many D6 we gotta roll when a rule tells us to roll multiple dice like 2D6 or 3D6, and what we do with them numbers?
reference: When some rules refer to 2D6, 3D6 and so on, you roll that many six-sided dice (D6) and add the results together.
reference_contexts:
DICE
In order to fight a battle, you will require some six-sided dice (often abbreviated to D6). Some rules refer to 2D6, 3D6 and so on - in such cases, roll that many D6 and add the results together.
If a rule requires you to roll a D3, roll a D6 and halve the result (rounding up to a whole number) to get the D3 result, as shown below.
DICE RESULT, ROLLING A D3 = D3 RESULT. or, ROLLING A D3 = 1. or, ROLLING A D3 = 2. or, ROLLING A D3 = 3
If a rule requires a dice roll of, for example, 3 or more, this is often abbreviated to 3+. Where several consecutive dice results are relevant to a rule, these are often shown as a range (e.g. 1-3).

user_input: Benefit of Cover rules ranged attacks saving throw
reference: Each time a ranged attack is allocated to a model that has the Benefit of Cover, you add 1 to the saving throw made for that attack, excluding invulnerable saving throws. However, models with a Save characteristic of 3+ or better cannot receive the Benefit of Cover against attacks with an Armour Penetration characteristic of 0, and multiple instances of the Benefit of Cover are not cumulative.
reference_contexts:
BENEFIT OF COVER
Shattered ruins and twisted wreckage afford much-needed shelter from enemy salvoes. Even heavily armoured warriors unfazed by small arms fire are thankful for such cover when foes bring their biggest guns to bear.
Models can sometimes gain a measure of protection from terrain features. The rules on pages 45-48 detail the conditions under which a terrain feature confers the Benefit of Cover on a model.
Each time a ranged attack is allocated to a model that has the Benefit of Cover, add 1 to the saving throw made for that attack (excluding invulnerable saving throws). Models with a Save characteristic of 3+ or better cannot have the Benefit of Cover against attacks with an Armour Penetration characteristic of 0. Multiple instances of the Benefit of Cover are not cumulative - a model cannot benefit from this rule more than once at any one time.
- ■ - Benefit of Cover: Add 1 to armour saving throws against ranged attacks.
- ■ - Does not apply to models with a Save of 3+ or better against attacks with an AP of 0.

user_input: How terrain features can affect when a unit fully visible or model fully visible for observing model?
reference: A unit is considered fully visible when every model in that unit is fully visible, meaning every facing part of a model can be seen. However, terrain features can block visibility, and for another model to be considered fully visible, no terrain features or other models can block visibility to any part of the model that is facing the observing model.
reference_contexts:
<1-hop>

UNIT FULLY VISIBLE
If every model in a unit is fully visible to an observing model, then that unit is fully visible to that observing model. For the purposes of determining if an enemy unit is fully visible, an observing model can see through other models in the unit it is observing.
- ■ - Model Visible: If any part of a model can be seen, it is visible.
- ■ - Unit Visible: If any model in a unit is visible, that model's unit is visible.
- ■ - Model Fully Visible: If every facing part of a model can be seen, it is fully visible.
- ■ - Unit Fully Visible: If every model in a unit is fully visible, that unit is fully visible.

<2-hop>

MODEL FULLY VISIBLE
If every part of another model that is facing the observing model can be seen from any part of the observing model, then that other model is said to be fully visible to the observing model, i.e. the observing model has line of sight to all parts of the other model that are facing it, without any other models or terrain features blocking visibility to any of those parts.

user_input: when a shooting unit selects a target unit, how do we resovle the attacks?
reference: When a shooting unit selects a target unit, you must resolve all of the attacks against one target before moving on to the next target. Additionally, you must resolve all attacks with the same weapon profile before resolving any made with a different weapon profile, and all attacks declared against a target unit are resolved even if no models in that unit remain within Engagement Range.
reference_contexts:
<1-hop>

MAKE RANGED ATTACKS
The shooting unit's models now make attacks using their ranged weapons. Each time a model shoots with a ranged weapon, it will make a number of attacks equal to the Attacks (A) characteristic in that weapon's profile. You make one Hit roll for each attack being made (see Making Attacks, pages 21-23).
If you selected more than one target for your unit to shoot at, you must resolve all of the attacks against one target before moving on to the next target. If your unit is shooting more than one ranged weapon at a target, and those weapons have different profiles, then after you have resolved attacks with one of those weapons you must, if any other weapons with the same profile are also being shot at that unit, resolve those attacks before resolving any other attacks against the target.

<2-hop>

MAKE ATTACKS
- ■ - Resolve all attacks against one unit before moving onto the next.
- ■ - Resolve all attacks with the same weapon profile before resolving any made with a different weapon profile.
- ■ - All attacks declared against a target unit are resolved, even if no models in that unit remain within Engagement Range.

user_input: During target selection, what specific conditions must be met to select an enemy unit, and how must attacks be resolved if you select targets?
reference: When you select targets before any attacks are resolved, you must ensure that at least one model in the enemy unit is both within range of the weapon (equal to or less than the weapon's Range characteristic) and visible to the attacking model. If you selected more than one target for your unit to shoot at, you must completely resolve all of the attacks against one target before moving on to the next target.
reference_contexts:
<1-hop>

MAKE RANGED ATTACKS
The shooting unit's models now make attacks using their ranged weapons. Each time a model shoots with a ranged weapon, it will make a number of attacks equal to the Attacks (A) characteristic in that weapon's profile. You make one Hit roll for each attack being made (see Making Attacks, pages 21-23).
If you selected more than one target for your unit to shoot at, you must resolve all of the attacks against one target before moving on to the next target. If your unit is shooting more than one ranged weapon at a target, and those weapons have different profiles, then after you have resolved attacks with one of those weapons you must, if any other weapons with the same profile are also being shot at that unit, resolve those attacks before resolving any other attacks against the target.

<2-hop>

SELECT TARGETS
Each time a unit shoots, before any attacks are resolved, you must select the enemy units that will be the targets for all of the ranged weapons you wish its models to make attacks with. Each time you select a target for a model's ranged weapon, you can only select an enemy unit as the target if at least one model in that unit is both within range of that weapon and visible to that attacking model (pg 8). An enemy model is within range of a weapon if the distance between it and the attacking model is equal to or less than that weapon's Range characteristic.
If a model has more than one ranged weapon, it can shoot all of them at the same target or it can shoot each of them at a different target, but it cannot split attacks from the same weapon across more than one target. Similarly, if a unit has more than one model, those models can shoot at the same or different targets. In any case, when you select a target unit you must declare which models will target that unit with which weapons before any attacks are resolved. If any of these weapons have more than one profile that you must choose between, you must also declare which profile is being used.

user_input: when rapid ingress let unit arrive like Reinforcements step of Movement, what rule govern movement phase Movement for unit already on battlefield first?
reference: During the Movement phase, you start by selecting one unit from your army on the battlefield to move. If the unit is not within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can make a Normal move, Advance, or Remain Stationary. If it is within Engagement Range of enemy models, it can either Remain Stationary or Fall Back. You repeat this for all units until all have moved, after which you progress to the Reinforcements step.
reference_contexts:
<1-hop>

1. MOVE UNITS
Start your Movement phase by selecting one unit from your army that is on the battlefield to move:
- ■ - Unless that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can make a Normal move, or Advance, or Remain Stationary.
- ■ - If that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can either Remain Stationary or Fall Back.
After you have finished moving that unit, select another unit from your army to move, and so on, until you have done so with all of your units. Once you have moved all of your units, progress to the Reinforcements step of your Movement phase.
